theorem exists_coefficient_construction (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]

title: Constructible exceptional coefficient construction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, and assume $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; no absolute separatedness is imposed on $X,Y$. For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ put $R_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $s$ range over finite stages $(E,n)$, integral stages $R_E$, rational stages $E$, and the closed stage $\Omega$. Write $\mathcal C_{T,s}=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ for the actual full coefficient categories: ordinary constant-ring pro-etale coefficients at finite stages, completed derived-complete coefficients with uniform finite-level Tor bounds at integral stages, raw scalar localization at rational stages, and common finite subfields of $\Omega$ at the closed stage [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. At ring stages write $I_{T,s}$ for the full inclusion into the ordinary derived category of the indicated coefficient sheaf.

There exists one family of normalized construction data, indexed by every compactification $c=(j,p_c)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], with the following fields (this is exactly the record $\mathrm{WeilConjectures.ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.CoefficientConstruction}(\ell,\Omega,D,\ell\ne p,f)$).

(1) For each $c,s$ there are additive exact functors $F^c_s:\mathcal C_{X,s}\to\mathcal C_{Y,s}$ and $G^c_s:\mathcal C_{Y,s}\to\mathcal C_{X,s}$ and an adjunction $F^c_s\dashv G^c_s$. Both functors have coherent integer-shift structures; its unit and counit commute with shifts. For each ring stage there is a realization $r_{c,s}:I_{Y,s}F^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rp_{c,*}j_!)I_{X,s}$ with the specified coefficient sheaf [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. At finite stages $I_{X,s}G^c_s\cong(\nu_X^*f^\times_{c,s}R\nu_{Y,*})I_{Y,s}$, the fixed finite exceptional construction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At integral stages a second left realization identifies $F^c_{R_E}$ with the prescribed reduction-tower compact-support functor [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; after inclusion its map is $r_{c,R_E}$ followed by the canonical ambient-to-tower realization. At rational stages $F^c_E$ is identified with the rationalization of that prescribed integral functor.

(2) An allowed ring coefficient change $a:s\to t$ is generated by finite quotients, the ramified finite maps $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}$ for an algebra embedding $E\to L$ of ramification index $e$, integral reduction $R_E\to A_{E,n}$, completed integral extension $R_E\to R_L$, identities with their actual identity ring maps, and composites whose actual ring-sheaf maps compose. For every such $a$ and $T=X,Y$ there is an additive exact scalar functor $T_{a,T}:\mathcal C_{T,s}\to\mathcal C_{T,t}$, with shift structure and realization $\theta_{a,T}:I_{T,t}T_{a,T}\cong S_{a,T}I_{T,s}$, where $S_{a,T}$ is ordinary derived extension along the actual coefficient-sheaf map [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a finite target choose the literal restriction of $S_{a,T}$, so the inclusion equality is an equality of functors and $\theta$ is its equality isomorphism. For an integral extension choose the published strict-tower scalar functor itself; $\theta^{-1}$ is the canonical completed scalar comparison from ordinary derived extension to that strict-tower functor. There are scalar identity and scalar composition isomorphisms whose images under the inclusions and $\theta$ are the multiplication unitor and balanced derived tensor associator.

(3) For every $c,a$ there are invertible shift-compatible maps
$$q^c_a:T_{a,Y}F^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_tT_{a,X},\qquad b^c_a:T_{a,X}G^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}G^c_tT_{a,Y}.$$
The image of $q^c_a$ under the scalar and left realizations is the canonical proper/open scalar-adjunction comparison for $Rp_{c,*}j_!$. The map $b^c_a$ is its counit-normalized transpose, namely
$$\epsilon^c_{t,T_{a,Y}L}\circ F^c_t(b^c_{a,L})\circ q^c_{a,G^c_sL}=T_{a,Y}(\epsilon^c_{s,L}).$$

(4) The raw rationalization functors and rational scalar-extension functors have shift structures and individual invertible shift-compatible $q,b$ with the same counit equation. The left rationalization comparison, composed with the rational left realization of (1), is exactly the raw localization of the integral left realization. On each integral representative the rational scalar $q$ is the raw localization of the integral scalar $q$. At the common-field inclusion for every finite subfield of $\Omega$, there are such $q,b$, and $q$ is the identity on the represented compact-support object.

(5) For every proper compactification refinement $u:c\to d$ and every stage $s$ there are shift-compatible natural isomorphisms $\alpha_{u,s}:F^c_s\cong F^d_s$ and $\rho_{u,s}:G^d_s\cong G^c_s$. They satisfy both adjunction equations
$$\epsilon^d_L\circ\alpha_{u,s,G^d_sL}=\epsilon^c_L\circ F^c_s(\rho_{u,s,L}),\qquad \rho_{u,s,F^d_sK}\circ\eta^d_K=G^c_s(\alpha_{u,s,K})\circ\eta^c_K.$$
At ring stages $\alpha$ is the proper/open refinement comparison through the left realizations: use the isomorphism $j_{d!}\cong Ru_*j_{c!}$ normalized by the open unit, then its inverse and proper direct-image composition. At rational stages it is the localization of the integral refinement map. Under the common-stage $q$ it is the image of the rational refinement map. These are the fields of the construction record; identity/composition equations for the $q,b$ families and for refinements are separate coherence obligations.

proof.text: Fix a compactification $c=(j,p_c)$. Proper finite type over the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ makes its middle scheme finite type over $k$; all three schemes are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. Choose a nonnegative dimension bound $d_c$ for the middle scheme using the finite-dimension theorem, and use $d_c=0$ when it is empty. For an input of Tor interval $[a,b]$, open extension preserves that interval and bounded constructibility, and the direct-image theorem applied to $p_c$ gives $F^c_{A}K=Rp_{c,*}j_!K$ in the finite-Tor category with interval $[a,b+2d_c]$. These constants depend on $c$, not the coefficient level. The termwise exact-functor and derived-direct-image theorems give the left functor its exact and shift structures.

source.place: Construction 2.17, Theorem 2.18, and Proposition 3.16(1); finite-stage compact support.

proof.text: On ordinary etale categories choose the compact-support right adjoint of thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint. The bounded-class adjunction theorem identifies its pro-etale transport with the specified composite $G^c_A=\nu_X^*f^\times_{c,A}R\nu_{Y,*}$ and gives a natural Hom bijection for all bounded-below etale-origin left inputs. Every bounded constructible input has that origin. The preservation corollary applies to this same composite and supplies bounded constructibility and a Tor interval independent of the finite level. Thus the bijections restrict to the actual full finite-Tor categories and give an adjunction there, with unit, counit and both triangles by the natural-bijection theorem. The ambient realization of $F$ and the finite-right realization are the inclusion identifications of these restrictions.

source.place: Proposition 2.23, Proposition 3.16(2), and the blueprint finite exceptional composite.

proof.text: The finite-Tor categories are triangulated by the finite-ctf theorem. Equip the right adjoint with the unique adjoint shift structure for the already chosen left shift structure. The shift-adjunction theorem gives compatibility of its unit and counit at every integer. Apply the triangulated-right-adjoint theorem, whose shift hypotheses are now satisfied, to obtain right exactness with these very shifts. Additivity of the right adjoint also follows directly from its Hom bijections: transposition respects sums because the left functor is additive. This constructs the finite-stage Operation fields, rather than assuming them.

source.place: Finite adjunction; exactness formalized by Stacks Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact.

proof.text: For a finite coefficient map $A\to B$, choose a bounded flat constructible etale model $P$ of a finite-Tor object. The flat-model theorem supplies it on our Noetherian schemes. Each $P^i\otimes_A B$ is flat over $B$: testing an injection of $B$-modules is testing the same injection after restriction to $A$. Its terms are finite locally constant on finite refinements of the strata trivializing the terms of $P$, so its cohomology is constructible. The complex still occupies $[a,b]$. Derived change of rings gives its map action, exactness and independence of model. Transport to the pro-etale category through constructible origin and the Tor comparison; exact inverse image commutes with this constant-ring tensor on the flat model. Define the scalar functor as the literal restriction of the ambient derived extension. Its realization is consequently the equality isomorphism required in finiteScalar_normalized, including composites of the allowed maps.

source.place: Finite-coefficient change of rings and bounded flat models; Proposition 2.29.

proof.text: At a finite ring map work first on etale categories. Take $q$ to be the proper/open scalar comparison specified by lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence, not an arbitrary isomorphism. It is invertible even for nonflat quotients. To identify the scalar restriction square use ordinary ringed direct-image composition, which applies also to the same topos with a changed ring; open extension commutes with restriction on the underlying complexes. This gives $\operatorname{Res}_YF_B\cong F_A\operatorname{Res}_X$. Together with the normalized derived scalar/restriction adjunction it fixes the scalar-adjunction mate. Thus this $q$ has exactly the realization equation CounitQNormalized at the finite stages.

source.place: Proper/open scalar comparison; see also Stacks more-etale.tex Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings.

proof.text:
Define $b_L$ as the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_Y\epsilon_{A,L}\circ q^{-1}_{G_AL}$. This immediately gives the required counit equation. Prove invertibility before restricting: the chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\operatorname{Res}_XG_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T_XK,G_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(F_BT_XK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T_YF_AK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,G_A\operatorname{Res}_YN)$$
identifies $\operatorname{Res}_XG_B$ with $G_A\operatorname{Res}_Y$ by Yoneda. With this identification, restriction of $b_L$ is the exceptional constant-$B$ tensor map: its transpose is inverse projection followed by $1\otimes\epsilon_A$. The constant-tensor lemma makes this specified map invertible for arbitrary $B\in D(A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$, including nonflat quotients. Restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms since the cohomology of its cone is the same underlying abelian sheaf. Hence $b_L$ is invertible as a $B$-linear map.

source.place: Propositions 2.23 and 2.29(2); constant-coefficient exceptional tensor map (2.26.1).

proof.text: Transport $q,b$ and the etale adjunction through the constructible-origin equivalence. The compact-support comparison and the Tor comparison identify the same $F,G$ on the finite full categories; the site-comparison unit is invertible on bounded-below complexes. Proper/open comparisons are the canonical adjunction mates, so the transported $q$ is the proper/open pro-etale scalar map in the realization equation. For its proper factor use the counit-normalized direct-image comparison; for its open factor use extension-zero comparison. The inverse-image/tensor identification is canonical on flat models by the derived pullback theorem. The counit-transpose description identifies the transported $b$ and counits, without choosing unrelated Hom bijections. Tensor comparisons, the proper projection mate and termwise open comparisons commute with shifts. Uniqueness of adjoint shifts then gives bShift for their transposes; composition and whiskering preserve these equations.

source.place: Tags 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible; 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; 09B1, lemma-compare-derived; finite proper/open adjunction mates.

proof.text: Form the actual strict systems with coefficients $A_n=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ on the etale site. The coefficient-system adjunction theorem gives an $R_E$-linear exact adjunction $\mathsf F^{et}=Rp_{c,A,*}j_{!,A}\dashv\mathsf G^{et}$ on their ordinary derived categories. Its conclusion supplies $e_n\mathsf G^{et}\cong f^\times_{c,A_n}e_n$, including evaluated units, counits and quotient transitions, a uniform lower bound and preservation of bounded-below normalization. These assertions are not inferred merely from evaluation of the left functor. Schemes have trivial inertia, and our geometric hypotheses are precisely those of that node; in particular $Y$ may be nonseparated. All further operations use this actual derived-system adjunction.

source.place: Construction 5.15, Lemmas 5.13, 5.16 and 5.22, and Proposition 5.24 (pp. 34–36).

proof.text:
Write $C_T=\nu^*_{T,A}$ and $V_T=R\nu_{T,A,*}$. The system comparison theorem supplies an actual adjunction with the stated evaluation isomorphisms. On bounded-below systems of etale-origin levels its counit is invertible; its unit is invertible because it evaluates to the finite site-comparison unit and evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms. These are equivalences on this class and preserve normalization. Construct the system compact-support comparison by the derived direct-image mate for the proper factor and the termwise open comparison. Evaluation gives the canonical proper and open comparisons, so joint conservativity proves that this actual system map is invertible. The system Hom chain is therefore
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathsf F^{pro}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathsf F^{et}V_XM,V_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V_XM,\mathsf G^{et}V_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,C_X\mathsf G^{et}V_YN).$$
Use its unit and counit to transport the adjunction and its finite coefficient transposes. No faithfulness of finite evaluations on morphisms is used.

source.place: Zheng Lemma 5.22 transported using system comparison; finite comparison is Stacks Tag 09B1.

proof.text: Use the reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$ of the derived-system evaluation calculus. Its unit is the actual compatible cone of quotient maps from one flat-term K-flat representative. The $L=E$ case of the finite-free completed-scalar comparison identifies that unit with the derived-completeness isomorphism for integral objects. On normalized systems its counit is invertible by normalized-DVR effectivity; the component is the scalar adjunct of the actual total-limit projection. Thus these functors restrict to mutually inverse equivalences between derived-complete objects and normalized systems, with the named unit and counit. Under the integral category definition, common constructible cohomological and Tor intervals on the levels are exactly the finiteness conditions needed for these equivalences to restrict to our integral finite-Tor subcategory.

source.place: Reduction and total-limit reconstruction; Zheng Section 4 and the explicit pro-etale effectivity nodes.

proof.text: Restrict the transported system adjunction to normalized systems of bounded constructible finite-Tor levels. The left bounds of Step 1 are uniform in $n$; the finite exceptional preservation corollary gives common right bounds, and the system theorem gives normalized right outputs. Define $F_R=\mathcal L_Y\mathsf F^{pro}\mathcal R_X$ and $G_R=\mathcal L_X\mathsf G^{pro}\mathcal R_Y$. Transport the actual unit and counit through the equivalences of Step 10; their triangles follow from the system triangles and those equivalences. The integral compact-support theorem identifies $F_R$ with the published reduction-tower functor and its specified reductions. The integral finite-Tor subcategory is triangulated. Reduction and total limit are exact, and the system adjunction is exact, so these are exact operations; alternatively apply the right-adjoint exactness theorem with the adjoint shifts. The unique adjoint shift structures give unitShift and counitShift.

source.place: Zheng Constructions 5.20 and 5.25, Proposition 5.24; normalized-system integral adjunction.

proof.text: Choose the integral left functor to be the prescribed reduction-tower compact-support functor, transporting the adjunction of Step 11 along its specified identification. The system-realization theorem applied to the single word $S_{p_c}J_j$ supplies its natural realization in the ambient completed-ring derived category, with the canonical proper/open maps. All intermediate objects satisfy its hypotheses by Step 1 and Step 11. Take $r_{c,R}$ to be the inverse of this ambient-to-tower realization after the integral-left identification. Then the included integralLeft map is, by this very choice, $r_{c,R}$ followed by the specified ambient-to-tower realization: this is integralLeft_normalized. This uses a realization of the actual system maps, rather than inferring equality of integral maps from finite evaluations. For the named integral realization and its maps, use the slotwise shift-realization theorem; it states compatibility with the canonical termwise and Roos-cone shifts for these same normalized expressions.

source.place: Single-compactification word realization; the published reduction-tower compact support and its proper/open maps.

proof.text: For integral reduction choose the literal restriction of ambient derived extension to $A_{E,n}$; its output is the reduction in the definition of the integral finite-Tor category. Step 10 identifies the reduction of $F_R,G_R$ with their evaluated system operations. Its unit and counit identify those comparisons with the system evaluation comparisons, hence the resulting $b$ is the counit transpose of $q$. The proper/open system realization identifies the left map with the ambient scalar mate, so comparison_normalized holds. Its component equations hold as maps before evaluation, since they are transported system adjunction equations. These comparisons commute with shifts by their derived constructions and the unique adjoint shift structures. For the named integral realization and its maps, use the slotwise shift-realization theorem; it states compatibility with the canonical termwise and Roos-cone shifts for these same normalized expressions.

source.place: Zheng Lemmas 5.16 and 5.22, with the reduction/limit unit and counit normalization.

proof.text: For an embedding $E\to L$, identify $E$ with its image and write $e$ for the ramification index. At selected levels $B_n=R_L/\varpi_E^nR_L=A_{L,en}$, use the finite-free system scalar comparison in the system adjunction theorem. To recover the full $L$-tower use the subsequence left-extension adjunction: for each $m$, choose the least $n$ with $en\ge m$ and form $A_{L,m}\otimes^L_{A_{L,en}}(-)_n$. On normalized systems its evaluation counit is the normalization isomorphism, so joint conservativity makes restriction and extension inverse equivalences. This transports the finite-free system comparisons to every level, on actual system maps. The same theorem gives the prescribed transition maps. Thus the scalar mate is invertible without replacing $en$ by $n$ or assuming that arbitrary derived evaluations are faithful.

source.place: Zheng Lemma 5.22; finite-free extension and cofinal ramified subsequences, with derived subsequence left extensions.

proof.text: Ordinary derived extension from $\widehat R_E$ to $\widehat R_L$ agrees with the published strict-tower integral scalar extension via the specified comparison $\chi_{L/E}$. It is an isomorphism, natural and complete, by the finite-free completed-scalar theorem. The constructibility and adic Tor-bound theorems supply the actual scalar functor on our subcategories, with the same common interval. Choose this published functor for integralScalar_eq, and choose $\theta=\chi^{-1}$ for its ambient realization; integralScalar_normalized now holds literally. Transport Step 14 and its counit-transpose equation through $\chi$ and the proper/open realization of Step 12. The left map is the canonical ambient scalar mate: on the ringed diagram site it is the proper scalar mate followed by the open tensor map, and the realization theorem intertwines these generator maps. This gives the integral $q,b$ and their required normalizations; the complete-scalar comparison and derived adjunction structures supply their shifts. For the named integral realization and its maps, use the slotwise shift-realization theorem; it states compatibility with the canonical termwise and Roos-cone shifts for these same normalized expressions.

source.place: Finite-free integral coefficient extension, Zheng Section 5; explicit completed-scalar comparison and diagram-site realization.

proof.text: For every allowed composite choose the same scalar functor as for its actual coefficient-sheaf map: the literal derived restriction for a finite target, and the published integral extension for an integral target. Derived balanced associativity identifies successive scalar extensions with that choice. On flat-term representatives the map is $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b(s)t$, and the identity map is $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$. Lift these through the full inclusions using $\theta$; this defines scalarComposition and scalarIdentity with exactly their ambient normalization equations. The proper scalar-mate cocycle on ringed diagram sites and the open-unit tensor normalization identify the composite $q$ with the mate for the composite ring map. Compose the $b$ maps with these associators: the counit equation follows by substitution of the two counit equations and naturality of $q$. Invertibility and shift compatibility survive composition. Thus the construction is defined for every Allowed witness, including identity and composite witnesses, and all q maps have comparison_normalized.

source.place: Canonical balanced scalar associativity and proper/open mate pasting; diagram-site comparisons before total limit.

proof.text: By the residue-Tor theorem every integral constructible representative belongs to the integral finite-Tor category. Localize the $R_E$-linear operations, natural transformations and adjunction Hom bijections at $\varpi_E$. The inverse localized Hom maps remain inverse because localization preserves the equations for their composites; the resulting unit, counit and triangles are their images. Raw scalar localization has the same objects and localized Hom modules, with exact localization functor. Hence the localized adjunction acts on exactly the published rational categories, and its operations and coefficient maps are exact with the induced shifts. Choose its left functor to be the published rational compact support and its rationalLeft realization to be the identity identification. This does not require a Karoubi completion.

source.place: Raw rational localization of the integral adjunction; blueprint coefficient construction.

proof.text: For integral-to-rational comparison take $q$ to be the localization of integralLeft followed by the inverse of rationalLeft. Take $b$ to be the identity comparison on the localized integral-right object, transported along those choices. The counit equation is the image of the integral one, so it has the required transpose normalization. For a rational embedding $E\to L$, define $q,b$ by localizing their integral versions on the same object representatives. On a morphism $h/\varpi_E^r$ use its localized image; the integral maps are linear and natural, so this is independent of representatives and natural. This gives exactly rationalization_normalized and rational_normalized: the left maps are the raw images of the indicated integral maps. The scalar-extension theorem and localized derived structures give the required endpoint shifts, and the comparisons preserve them.

source.place: Rationalization and rational coefficient comparisons, on the prescribed integral representatives.

proof.text: Define the closed-stage operations on a pair $(E,K)$ by $(E,F_EK)$ and $(E,G_EK)$. For a map represented over $L$ use its image under $F_L$ or $G_L$, conjugated by the scalar comparisons. The left transition identities follow from canonical tensor associativity and proper/open mate pasting of Step 16. For the right transitions, take the inverse transposes of the two composites: substitution of the counit equations reduces equality to the left transition identity. Injectivity gives equality. Therefore passage to a larger common field preserves these represented maps, composition and identities. Likewise the Hom bijections commute with transition maps, so inverse natural bijections pass to the directed colimit defining the closed coefficient category. Use them for the adjunction. Distinguished triangles and shifts are represented over one finite field, which gives exactness. On the inclusion of a finite common field take $q$ to be the identity on $(E,F_EK)$; take $b$ to be its counit transpose. This is the identity on $(E,G_E L)$ by the finite-field adjunction. These choices give common_normalized and the required shifts.

source.place: Common finite-field construction and third Hom bijection of sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom.

proof.text: For a proper refinement $u:c\to d$ at finite coefficients use the canonical comparison $\alpha:F^c\cong F^d$ of compactification coherence. Its source map is the inverse of $j_{d!}\cong Ru_*j_{c!}$ followed by proper composition. The etale definition normalizes this open map by the open-unit transpose of the clopen-section restriction isomorphism. Transport along the canonical site comparisons of Step 7; they are adjunction mates, so the open unit and proper counit remain the named ones. This is exactly RingRefinementNormalized at finite coefficients. On strict systems use the same proper/open map in the system realization theorem and take its total-limit realization. The theorem intertwines open units, proper counits and direct-image composition before total limit; hence, under $r_{c,R},r_{d,R}$, it gives RingRefinementNormalized at the integral stage as well. Its intermediate bounds follow from Step 11. These maps commute with shifts because the generator maps do. For the named integral realization and its maps, use the slotwise shift-realization theorem; it states compatibility with the canonical termwise and Roos-cone shifts for these same normalized expressions.

source.place: Proper/open compactification refinement, with open-unit and proper-counit normalization; Stacks Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined.

proof.text: Define $\rho:G^d\to G^c$ to be the $F^c\dashv G^c$ transpose of $\epsilon^d\circ\alpha_{G^d}$, and its inverse as the transpose using $\alpha^{-1}$. Substituting the counit equations, naturality of $\alpha$ and the triangle identities shows their composites transpose to the original counits, so they are inverse by injectivity. This proves the displayed refinement counit equation. For the unit equation, transpose its left side to $\epsilon^d_{F^dK}\circ\alpha_{G^dF^dK}\circ F^c\eta^d_K=\alpha_K$, using naturality and the $d$ triangle. Transpose its right side to $\alpha_K$ using the $c$ triangle. This proves the second equation. The unique-adjoint shift theorem makes $\rho$ shift-compatible with the shifts already chosen. At rational stages define $\alpha,\rho$ by localization of these maps; at the closed stage take their common-field representatives.
